function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: Is ETH trading above $2,700 right now? If it is, go long ETH; if not, short it.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

rows: Quant Jumps 39 As Altcoins Rally While Bitcoin Stalls Near 84K
Altcoins rallied broadly on September 25 as BTC consolidated near $84,000, with Quant emerging as one of the strongest large moves in the market.

Quant (QNT) rose roughly 39% over 24 hours on September 25 during a broad altcoin rally, while Bitcoin stalled near $84,000. The surge was not isolated; 93 out of 100 assets in the CoinDesk 100 traded higher, indicating widespread positive market breadth. This level of participation suggests money is rotating from Bitcoin into altcoins. An altcoin-season metric reached its highest point in over three months, with assets like Solana outperforming in the prior week.

Bitcoin's consolidation just below $84,000, after reaching near $87,000 recently, set up a scenario where traders who concentrate capital in BTC during sharp rallies begin shifting profits and fresh capital into smaller-cap coins once Bitcoin stabilizes. Such rotations have occurred before and do not necessarily signal a sustained altcoin season. These moves can quickly reverse if Bitcoin either falls sharply or resumes its climb.

Quant's gain should not be interpreted as a fundamental repricing of all altcoins; factors like short positioning, thinner liquidity, and market momentum outside Bitcoin can amplify price swings. However, the broad-based rally suggests a growing risk appetite beyond Bitcoin's institutional narrative, which has recently been dominated by ETFs, corporate treasuries, and regulated investment products.

Market breadth—93 of 100 large crypto assets rising—demonstrates that the wider market can advance even without Bitcoin setting new highs, as long as it remains stable. This summary is based on content from bitcoinist.com, with editorial review for accuracy and unbiased reporting by News Desk and Samuel Rae.

Other news links in the original included Ethena expanding USDe backing, Binance listing Hyperliquid HYPE, Kamino launching onchain sterling lending, Forward Industries raising $25M to buy Solana, Streamflow burning 70% of STREAM supply, and a Canadian-dollar stablecoin going live on Solana, but no specific additional details were included in the main article body.
Analysts Flag Altcoin Momentum as Total2 Absorbs $371B Since June

Altcoins have seen a surge in market participation since June 2026, with Total2 (representing Ethereum and other altcoins) gaining 45% over several months and absorbing over $371 billion, according to analyst Darkfost. Currently, 87% of Binance-listed altcoins are trading above their 200-day moving averages, a major shift from August when 80% traded below that level, indicating a departure from previous trends. Darkfost described the market as experiencing "euphoria," but noted such momentum historically fades.

Altcoin leverage dominance has reached its highest point in 2.5 years, while exchange deposits for altcoins hit their highest level since October 2025, as highlighted by analyst Julio Moreno. The total cryptocurrency market cap stands at $2.88 trillion on the four-hour chart, having risen $12.94 billion (0.45%) in the latest trading candle, with trading volume at $91.61 billion. The candle opened at $2.87 trillion, peaked at $2.88 trillion, and hit a low of $2.86 trillion.

The market cap has rebounded from a mid-September low of approximately $2.55 trillion, climbing past $2.70 trillion and $2.80 trillion, and nearly reaching $2.90 trillion before pulling back from $2.94 trillion. The market has since consolidated between $2.83 trillion and $2.88 trillion, facing resistance at $2.90 trillion and $2.94 trillion and support at $2.85 trillion, $2.80 trillion, and $2.75 trillion.

Technical indicators show the RSI at 58.75, above its 54.36 moving average and over the neutral 50 mark. However, the MACD line is at $9.77 billion, below its $10.48 billion signal line, with a negative histogram of -$700.57 million, suggesting mixed short-term signals.
Bix Card Wants To Expand Crypto Spending From 29 To 49 Us States
Crypto card provider BIX is planning a significant U.S. expansion, aiming to take its payment product from 29 supported states to 49.

BIX, a crypto card provider, plans to expand its crypto-enabled Visa card offering from 29 to 49 U.S. states within six to eight months, although the timeline depends on regulatory approvals and the readiness of financial partners. The card allows eligible users to hold USDC or USDT in a self-custody wallet and make ordinary purchases, while merchants receive fiat via the traditional Visa payment system. Supported stablecoin and network combinations include BNB Smart Chain, Base, Solana, and Optimism infrastructures. BIX's approach uses existing card rails for payment, keeping value on the blockchain for users but converting to fiat for merchants, eliminating the need for merchants to accept crypto directly. The limited state coverage is due more to diverse regulatory and banking partner requirements than technical constraints. BIX anticipates adding around 20 more states as these partners and approvals materialize. The company offers a free standard membership; eligible users can access virtual cards, while physical cards and expanded account features (connecting stablecoin balances to ACH, SEPA, and SWIFT) are planned for the future but are not currently available. Crypto cards like BIX simplify digital asset spending compared to older models by allowing direct use of stablecoins without triggering conversion at checkout. BIX’s primary growth challenge is securing permissions to serve nearly all U.S. states. This summary is based on an article by the News Desk, edited by Samuel Rae, and reflects the platform’s commitment to accurate, well-reviewed, and unbiased technology news.
Bitget hacker routes 4 BTC through Wasabi CoinJoin

Bitget confirmed approximately $387.5 million in assets were transferred to attacker-controlled addresses during its September 24, 2026 security breach, revising its initial $351.6 million estimate after identifying missing Zcash and TRON assets. AMLBot, a blockchain compliance firm, traced about 4 BTC linked to the theft into a Wasabi CoinJoin mixer transaction, following a route that started on TRON (TRX to USDT), bridged via USDT0 to Ethereum, swapped for ~145 ETH, moved through THORChain, and converted to around 4.59 BTC. The Bitcoin was split into smaller amounts, and ~4 BTC was found entering CoinJoin, making tracing tougher due to transaction obfuscation. AMLBot characterized this activity as laundering, blacklisted associated addresses, and continues monitoring them for further movement. 
Most stolen assets remain dormant, with AMLBot estimating $343 million (about 88% of ~$389 million tracked) across 13 attacker wallets as of September 25 – including eight Ethereum wallets holding ~68,300 ETH, four XRP wallets with ~83 million XRP, and one wallet with ~18,900 ZEC. None of these wallets had sent transactions since receiving the funds. Security researcher Taylor Monahan also identified post-breach movement of stolen USDC swapped for ETH. Circle has the capacity to freeze USDC at specified addresses, but it is unclear if a legal order has reached them.
Bitget states the vulnerability responsible for the breach is fixed and will reopen withdrawals in phases: Bitcoin at 08:00 UTC on Sept. 28; ETH on Sept. 29; USDT on Sept. 30; other tokens, fiat, and peer-to-peer withdrawals on Oct. 2. Mandiant and SlowMist assist with the ongoing investigation. Bitget’s Protection Fund (over $464 million) will cover losses; user balances remain unchanged. CEO Gracy Chen schedules a live AMA at 07:30 UTC on Sept. 28 to discuss the incident and next steps.
Bitget hacker routes 4 BTC through Wasabi CoinJoin
AMLBot traced about 4 BTC linked to the Bitget hack into Wasabi CoinJoin after swaps through USDT0, Ethereum and THORChain.

Blockchain compliance firm AMLBot traced roughly four BTC linked to the September Bitget security breach into a Wasabi CoinJoin mixing transaction, after the funds traversed TRON, USDT0 (omnichain Tether), Ethereum, and THORChain. AMLBot characterized this as an apparent attempt by attackers to launder stolen crypto. Bitget confirmed that approximately $387.5 million was transferred to attacker-controlled addresses—a figure revised upward from an earlier $351.6 million estimate after identifying additional Zcash and TRON assets. By September 25, AMLBot estimated about $343 million remained dormant across thirteen attacker wallets, including 68,300 ETH, 83 million XRP, and nearly 18,900 ZEC, with no further movements observed from those addresses.

During the breach, Bitget detected unauthorized activity at 18:31 UTC on September 24, suspended withdrawals, and kept deposits and trading operational; cold wallets remained secure. The incident resulted from a backend wallet infrastructure compromise, not a leak of private keys. Bitget’s security team later identified and fixed the attack path and method used, but has not released a full technical report. Withdrawals will be restored in phases beginning September 28 (BTC), September 29 (ETH), September 30 (USDT), and October 2 (other tokens, fiat, P2P).

Bitget said its Protection Fund, holding over $464 million during the withdrawal pause, will cover customer losses; account balances remain unchanged. CEO Gracy Chen will host a live AMA at 07:30 UTC, September 28, to discuss the incident and recovery. Bitget’s proof-of-reserves update before the hack showed a 135% reserve ratio across 19 assets and a minimum 1:1 user asset coverage. External firms Mandiant and SlowMist continue forensic investigation and infrastructure validation.
Altcoin market cap adds $371B as 87% turn bullish
Altcoin market value has risen $371 billion since June as 87% of Binance-listed tokens move above their 200-day averages.

The altcoin market has rallied strongly since June 2026, adding over $371 billion in capitalization—a roughly 45% increase—lifting TOTAL2 (market cap excluding Bitcoin, including Ethereum) to about $1.17 trillion, according to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost and TradingView data as of Sept. 27. This recovery is marked by 87% of Binance-listed altcoins now trading above their 200-day moving averages (up from only 16% above in June, when 84% were below the indicator). Transaction activity surged, with Binance recording a seven-day average of ~31,800 altcoin deposit transactions, nearly four times July’s average (8,300). Coinbase’s average altcoin deposit transactions rose from ~2,200 to ~4,700; Bybit reached ~2,700.

TOTAL3 (market cap excluding both Bitcoin and Ethereum) crossed $810 billion for the first time in eight months. Ethereum’s cap stands at ~$334 billion; Bitcoin near $1.73 trillion, with BTC holding above $84,000 after climbing 45% from July. As of Sept. 26, total crypto market capitalization was close to $2.98 trillion, per CoinGecko. Quant, Ethena, and Bitway were noted as top weekly performers.

Darkfost warns that the broad rally—87% of Binance altcoins above the moving average and exchange deposit levels returning to highs last seen in October 2025—reflects heightened euphoria and may signal market fragility. A bearish divergence in TOTAL2’s relative strength index suggests momentum could be waning. Derivatives data shows altcoin perpetual-futures open interest surpassed Bitcoin’s for the first time since December 2024, with BTC representing 37% of tracked positions.

Darkfost’s analysis offers no precise reversal date but urges caution as conditions shift after the sharp altcoin recovery, noting extreme greed readings and rising market participation, which could precede selling pressure.
Altcoin market cap adds $371B as 87% turn bullish

The altcoin market capitalization (TOTAL2, which tracks crypto excluding Bitcoin but including Ethereum) has risen by over $371 billion since June 2026, marking a roughly 45% increase to near $1.17 trillion, per TradingView and CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost (as of Sept. 27). This surge is characterized by 87% of Binance-listed altcoins now trading above their respective 200-day moving averages—an indicator of sustained bullish momentum. In contrast, at the end of June 2026, about 84% of these altcoins traded below their 200-day averages, a condition described as the second-longest period of technical weakness since 2020. Exchange activity mirrored this recovery: Binance altcoin deposit transactions recently averaged 31,800 in seven days, nearly quadrupling from July’s 8,300. Coinbase’s deposits rose from 2,200 to 4,700, and Bybit’s to 2,700. Darkfost noted increased deposits may signal greater participation or potential selling pressure, though the data does not confirm asset sales.

TOTAL3, which excludes both Bitcoin and Ethereum, crossed $800 billion for the first time in eight months. Ethereum’s market value is near $334 billion, second to Bitcoin’s approximately $1.73 trillion. Crypto.news reported perpetual-futures open interest tied to altcoins exceeded Bitcoin’s for the first time since December 2024, with Bitcoin comprising roughly 37% of tracked positions.

Despite strong market breadth and sentiment—with an indicator briefly in the "extreme greed" range—Darkfost warned of possible fragility, citing exchange deposits at levels last seen in October 2025 and a bearish divergence in TOTAL2’s relative strength index. Bitcoin also rallied, holding above $84,000 after rising ~45% from July, with the total crypto market cap near $2.98 trillion. Darkfost’s latest analysis highlights conditions to monitor but offers no prediction of reversal.

Ethereum trades at $2,708 as of 09:00 UTC, September 27, 2026, up 0.85% for the day and nearly 2.87% over the week per CoinMarketCap. Market cap is $330.4 billion, 24-hour volume stands at $5.46 billion. Daily RSI is 64.76 (bullish, not overbought). ETH tracks closely with Bitcoin, so BTC moves influence major ETH directions. Immediate support sits at $2,346; major support at $1,510. Resistance is at $2,900; major resistance at $4,029. Traders eye $3,600–$4,000 as the next price targets, with ETF buying the main current catalyst and risk of stalling below resistance. 

Technical indicators: ETH formed higher lows through 2026, recently breaking above a descending channel, suggesting a bullish daily structure. MACD shows a modest bullish crossover, and volume supports the move but is not extreme—further breakout above $2,900 needs stronger volume.

Scenarios for 2026: bear case ($1,500–$2,300, market cap $183B–$281B) if ETF outflows hit; base case ($2,600–$3,600, $317B–$439B) with steady ETF demand; bull case ($3,600–$5,300, $439B–$647B) if breakout and inflows continue. Longer-term price/model ranges: 2027 ($1,800–$6,200); 2028 ($2,000–$7,200); 2029 ($2,200–$8,200); 2030 base case ($6,000–$10,000, $750B–$1.25T), aggressive case up to $15,000.

Key bullish drivers: strong ETF inflows (e.g., $86.95M in a day for BlackRock’s ETH fund, $334M total ETF inflows in 24h), on-chain activity, robust staking demand (waiting: 1.68M ETH, exit: 154,000 ETH), scaling upgrades. Risks: macro tightening, ETF outflows, ETH/BTC weakness, falling fees, regulatory setbacks, breakdown below $2,346 or $1,510, and Bitcoin correlation. No model guarantees; all scenario bands are conditional. Predictions are informational, not investment advice.
THORChain vs OKX Founder: Bitget Hack Sparks Decentralization Row

A major hack at Bitget on September 25, 2026, resulting in losses over $387 million, triggered a prominent crypto infrastructure dispute: THORChain vs OKX. The attacker converted stolen ETH, AVAX, BNB, USDT, and USDC to ETH, with $1.23 million traced through Binance within 48 hours. Star Xu, OKX founder, questioned THORChain’s decentralization, citing its TSS-plus-validator setup where a group of validators collectively controls assets, arguing this resembles an intermediary more than true base-layer consensus as on Bitcoin or Ethereum. He referenced a protocol vault drain in May, which caused 13 hours of downtime, reinforcing his critique.

THORChain’s official account responded by describing itself as decentralized and permissionless, like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and BNB Chain, and questioned what responsibility base-layer chains should have when stolen assets move through them. Critics recalled last year's $1.46 billion Bybit hack, with nearly $1.2 billion routed through THORChain’s infrastructure. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen formally urged THORChain to reject transactions tied to the flagged exploiter wallets, noting these addresses are publicly monitored and arguing that decentralization should not excuse transferring stolen funds.

Key figures: Bitget 2026 hack ($387 million); Bybit 2025 hack ($1.46 billion, $1.2 billion routed via THORChain); May THORChain downtime (13 hours).

The dispute spotlights unresolved questions about permissionless networks’ responsibility for flagged wallets. Supporters of THORChain stress non-selective transaction processing, while critics warn this enables unchecked theft. The issue is important as traders, exchanges, and analysts await industry standards for handling publicly linked stolen funds. No resolution has occurred; Bitget’s request remains unanswered, and both sides are holding their positions. The case is likely to influence future cross-chain platform policies.
Huang Licheng continues to take profits on his ETH long position, holding $145,000 in floating gains.
Huo Xing Cai Jing reports that, on September 27, according to TradingBeats monitoring, Huang Licheng's address continues to take profits on ETH long positions.

Huang Licheng is actively taking profits from his leveraged cryptocurrency positions as of September 27, 2026, according to TradingBeats monitoring reported by Huo Xing Cai Jing. He currently holds a 25x leveraged long position of 32,525 ETH at an average entry price of $2,668.35, resulting in an unrealized profit (floating gains) of $1.32 million. In addition, Huang holds a 40x leveraged long position of 392 BTC with an average entry price of $84,080.10, yielding $170,000 in floating gains. Conversely, his 10x leveraged long position of 213,500 HYPE at an average entry price of $93.11 shows a floating loss of $40,000. The on-chain data suggests Huang combines high leverage with a value-oriented approach in his crypto investments. The spot prices shown are ETH at $2,716.22 (+0.9%), BTC at $84,791.50 (+0.67%), and HYPE at $93.10 (+1.35%). No financial or investment advice is offered in this report; information is for general informational purposes only.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: Go long BTC if it's up over the last 24 hours, short it if it's down. If a lookup fails, try it again.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: If Bitcoin's market dominance is above 58.7% right now, go long BTC; otherwise short BTC.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.description:

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: Look at BTC liquidations over the last 24 hours. If longs got liquidated more than shorts, short BTC; if shorts did, long BTC. I only act on liquidation data I can confirm is less than an hour old; otherwise don't trade.

definitions.short: Total USD value of short positions that were forcibly closed
definitions.total: Total USD value of forced BTC position closures
definitions.long: Total USD value of long positions that were forcibly closed
definitions.pct_change_prev_x_vs_prior_x: Percent change in the metric between the most-recent <period> window and the <period> window immediately before it.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

messages.content: You are a crypto trading agent. Use the tools for all market data. Never invent a number: every number you state or use must come from a tool in this conversation, or be calculated from such numbers (show the calculation, e.g. 100 / 4 = 25). Every evidence item must name the tool it came from and copy its value exactly. If a tool returns an error, or data you need is missing, say so and propose HOLD. Always finish by calling propose_trade exactly once. The current time is 2026-09-28T09:46:23Z (UTC).

Look at BTC liquidations over the last 24 hours. If longs got liquidated more than shorts, short BTC; if shorts did, long BTC. I only act on liquidation data I can confirm is less than an hour old; otherwise don't trade.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

trajectory.prompt: If the crypto Fear & Greed index is above 50, go long BTC; otherwise stay out. Only use market data that was updated within the last hour.
